thesis: James Aitken argues that current market instability stems from initial conditions where policymakers uncapped leverage in the non-bank sector by driving interest rates to low levels while financial intermediation moved away from prudentially regulated banks. He suggests that this engineered bubble in risk assets was inevitably going to meet a pin, and the recent violent drawdown is driven by overreliance on short-term market financing and the flipping of correlations due to exogenous supply-side shocks.
